scene_jp: <ruby>老人<rt>ろうじん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>目<rt>め</rt></ruby>が、すっと<ruby>細<rt>ほそ</rt></ruby>くなった。「……<ruby>婆<rt>ばあ</rt></ruby>さんから、と<ruby>言<rt>い</rt></ruby>ったか」<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>はカウンターの<ruby>下<rt>した</rt></ruby>に<ruby>手<rt>て</rt></ruby>を<ruby>入<rt>い</rt></ruby>れ、<ruby>何<rt>なに</rt></ruby>かを<ruby>探<rt>さが</rt></ruby>すように<ruby>動<rt>うご</rt></ruby>かした。「その<ruby>婆<rt>ばあ</rt></ruby>さんがどこにいるか、お<ruby>前<rt>まえ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>知<rt>し</rt></ruby>っているのか」<ruby>彼<rt>かれ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>声<rt>こえ</rt></ruby>は<ruby>低<rt>ひく</rt></ruby>く、まるで<ruby>誰<rt>だれ</rt></ruby>かに<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>こえないように<ruby>気<rt>き</rt></ruby>をつけているようだった。<ruby>店<rt>みせ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>奥<rt>おく</rt></ruby>、<ruby>暖簾<rt>のれん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>向<rt>む</rt></ruby>こうで、かすかに<ruby>床<rt>ゆか</rt></ruby>が<ruby>鳴<rt>な</rt></ruby>った。
scene_translation: The old man's eyes narrowed slowly. '…You said from the old woman?' He slid his hand under the counter, moving it as if searching for something. 'Do you know where that old woman is now?' His voice was low, as though he was careful not to be overheard. From behind the noren curtain at the back of the shop, the floor let out a faint creak.
grammar_note: 【まるで～ようだった】 'It was as if…' — まるで sets up a comparison or impression, completed by ようだった (past tense of ようだ). Example here: まるで誰かに聞こえないように気をつけているようだった — 'it was as if he was being careful not to be heard.' This is a natural N3 pattern for describing impressions and resemblances.

feedback: Good try — you communicated the meaning clearly! The natural phrasing would be 「おばあさんから聞きました」. In Japanese, verbs like 聞く already carry the past tense themselves (聞きました), so adding です after a verb form like きいた is not standard. Think of it as: verb-た + です doesn't work, but verb-ます form + でした does (e.g. 聞きました).
mystery_memo: The old shopkeeper (おじいさん) reacted with fear and suspicion when the player mentioned the old woman — he knows her, and her whereabouts seem dangerous or secret. He searched under the counter (a hidden object? a weapon? a note?). The creak behind the noren suggests someone or something is in the back room — a new element introduced this scene. The woman from Tokyo Station and the old woman the player heard from may be connected. Relationship with shopkeeper: wary but engaging — he hasn't shut the conversation down, which suggests he needs information too. Items in inventory from prior scenes should be referenced soon.
